validated_results.title: A prospective study of dietary alpha-linolenic acid and the risk of prostate cancer (United States).
validated_results.reason: Prospective cohort of PLCO men reporting dietary alpha-linolenic acid intake and incident prostate cancer risk estimates.

extraction.comparison_type: highest vs lowest quintile of total ALA intake
extraction.population: male participants aged 55-74 years in the screening arm of the PLCO Cancer Screening Trial

sample_size.excerpt: A cohort of 29,592 male participants (age 55-74 years) in the screening arm of the Prostate, Lung, Colorectal, and Ovarian (PLCO) Cancer Screening Trial was followed for an average of 5.1 years. We ascertained 1,898 cases of total prostate cancer, of which 1,631 were organ-confined cases (stage T1b to T3a and N0M0) and 285 were advanced stage cases (stage>or=T3b, N1, or M1).

cases.excerpt: We ascertained 1,898 cases of total prostate cancer, of which 1,631 were organ-confined cases (stage T1b to T3a and N0M0) and 285 were advanced stage cases (stage>or=T3b, N1, or M1).

effect_size.excerpt: We ascertained 1,898 cases of total prostate cancer, of which 1,631 were organ-confined cases (stage T1b to T3a and N0M0) and 285 were advanced stage cases (stage>or=T3b, N1, or M1). We found no association between total ALA intake and overall prostate cancer (multivariate RR comparing extreme quintiles=0.94; 95% CI=0.81-1.09; P for trend=0.76).

confidence_interval.excerpt: We found no association between total ALA intake and overall prostate cancer (multivariate RR comparing extreme quintiles=0.94; 95% CI=0.81-1.09; P for trend=0.76).
